cases.abstract: Opinion panels can resemble partner drift or persistence when exposure is unobserved. We evaluate a synthetic detection boundary for a fixed lag-based discriminator against matched no-network persistence. An eleven-wave rank-transported autoregression combines bounded-confidence-shaped drift and an unobserved random network; first-order drift depends on individual state. Panels use Swiss Household Panel geometry and a response signal share known to both arms. Nulls match short-lag population moments. The primary estimand is the curve of first grid strengths whose expected AUC against trait-plus-autoregressive persistence reaches 0.70. Evaluation used new seeds after partial calibration exposure and protocol amendment. The gate passed; \resultnum{v4.inv.n_valid}{45} of 414 units finished valid. On \resultnum{v4.bd.n_eligible}{9} shared gap-free shares ($r=$ \resultnum{v4.bd.r_eligible}{0.50, 0.55, 0.60, 0.65, 0.70, 0.75, 0.80, 0.85, 0.90}), first boundaries against trait-plus-autoregressive/state-dependent persistence were small \resultnum{v4.bd.B.n_small}{9}/\resultnum{v4.bd.D.n_small}{0}, large \resultnum{v4.bd.B.n_large}{0}/\resultnum{v4.bd.D.n_large}{0}, not attained \resultnum{v4.bd.B.n_not_attained}{0}/\resultnum{v4.bd.D.n_not_attained}{9}, or censored/indeterminate \resultnum{v4.bd.B.n_censored}{0}/\resultnum{v4.bd.D.n_censored}{0}. At \resultnum{v4.bd.n_persistence}{9} of those shares this is compatible with non-Gaussian persistence, without specific evidence of interaction. Separation is conditional on the declared laws, response channel and discriminator and does not identify causal social influence.

cases.discussion:
% Revised 2026-09-28 after the pre-results referee report. Markers DSxx map to
% rows in claim-evidence.md, section "Discussion (integrated 2026-09-28)".
% Open exploratory X5 estimates are stated; no confirmatory outcome is asserted.
% DS01
The primary interpretation is conditional on the specified null family, response channel, panel design and fixed lag-feature discriminator. Attained boundaries on a complete valid curve will carry the frozen v1 labels: a small boundary ($0<a^*\le0.03$) would mean that this discriminator separates the declared synthetic laws at a small nominal strength, and a large one ($0.03<a^*\le0.90$) that separation requires a strength farther along the grid; the cut at 0.03 is an internal convention, not a demonstrated effect size. A complete valid noncrossing would mean only that this discriminator did not attain the target on that grid; it would leave stronger inputs, other summaries and other classifiers unresolved. Gaps, edges or wide intervals make the affected region censored or indeterminate, and a zero-strength band that misses 0.5 invalidates the comparison at that value of $r$. Point crossings followed by lower AUCs must be distinguished from sustained crossings. Statements about how the boundary changes across $r$ are descriptive. No part of the curve identifies causal influence in a panel without observed exposure.

% DS02
The headline will report the comparisons against B and against D side by side whenever tier 2 is complete and valid. This pairing matters because, to first order, partner drift is a nonlinear function of a person's own state that pushes people away from the population centre, more strongly in the tails, so that after rank transport the interaction arm is a state-dependent persistence process, the class that D targets with a different functional form (Methods). If B crosses while D's valid upper band remains below the target, the frozen reading is that the result is compatible with non-Gaussian persistence and gives no specific evidence of interaction; a band spanning the target is inconclusive. A nonsignificant contrast does not establish equivalence. If tier 2 is incomplete at the close, the paper reports only the comparison against B and makes no cross-mechanism statement.

% DS03
The estimand is an oracle quantity. Both arms share a known signal share, so the null cannot adjust the response-channel noise variance. Estimation difficulties have been reported for trait--state--error decompositions \cite{cole2005tso,ludtke2018starts}. Each null is matched to population moments averaged over many simulated panels, not to one observed panel. The AUC target of 0.70 corresponds, under normal-theory assumptions, to a single-panel power of only about 0.18 (Table~\ref{tab:auc-translation}). A boundary is therefore a property of two laws at a known signal share, not a statement that an analyst holding one panel would detect partner drift at that strength. Both arms also have time-invariant parameters and marginals, although the interaction arm starts without burn-in, and they share an exact response channel, mask and marginal, with attrition unrelated to opinion. Real panels can violate this through attrition related to the item, reliability that varies across waves, changes of mode or wording, period shocks and refreshment samples of different composition, any of which could by itself make two panel laws separable. % DS03 RC17

The X5 misspecification comparison is unavailable in this artificial package because no X5 aggregate was supplied. This absence is not a null result.

% DS04
The generator is one fixed configuration: persistence 0.85, repulsion 0.25, eight random partners, no burn-in and one step per wave, with only attraction-only, anchoring and 24-step variants. Its rank transport removes the population-level signatures of bounded-confidence and repulsion models, so the boundary is not transferable to those models as usually understood. The interaction arm's lag profile has not been compared with that of the SHP item, so the panels share the survey's geometry but not necessarily its persistence. The SHP also records household co-residence, and household members aged 14 and older complete individual questionnaires \cite{voorpostel2025shp}; a household-coupled generator with a dyadic discriminator is left to future work.

% DS05
The SHP reliability anchor and the simulation's $r$ are different quantities. The anchor treats the 0--10 responses as continuous, whereas $r$ is a signal share before rank-based discretization. The anchor model is a latent autoregression without a stable trait, whereas null B has one; when a trait is present, simplex-type estimators attribute part of the long-lag plateau to the autoregression. For example, with latent lag correlations $0.5+0.5\cdot0.5^k$ and $r=0.70$, the Heise triplet estimate is about 0.63. The anchor wave, 2004, is the year the SHP added its first refreshment sample \cite{voorpostel2025shp}, which is also wave five of the synthetic geometry, so that wave mixes first interviews with continuing respondents. The anchor's interval is a model-based Wald interval, not a design-based one. The raw quasi-simplex anchor, the STARTS sensitivity and the synthetic compatibility map must therefore be presented separately. % DS05 RC24
The map depends on generator, strength and trait--state composition; its minimum--maximum ranges over ten synthetic replicates are not confidence intervals and do not propagate uncertainty in the empirical anchor. % DS05 RC25
It does not yield an empirically calibrated $a^*(r)$. % DS05 RC26

% DS06
Absolute interior coverage of the bands is not verified. The zero-strength gates test band mechanics where the nulls are exact by construction; G1b uses zero nuisance variance; G2 tests dispersion only; matching bias up to a quarter of the fitting standard error lies outside the variance; and the criteria's calibrated joint pass probability is not shown to reach 0.95. If the nine zero-strength gates of the main curve are independent and the procedure is correct, chance alone gives the main curve a probability of invalidation of up to about 5\%, in addition to invalidation by the compute close.

% DS07
The protocol was amended after partial calibration exposure, particularly at $r=0.70$. New seeds and sealed gate records constrain further adaptation but cannot make the resulting evaluation fully blind. Results at the other values of $r$ remain part of the prespecified whole curve; they cannot erase the method-level exposure. The v4 finite-law equality at zero strength is an identity of this simulator and random-number coupling. It does not imply equality of empirical mechanisms or guarantee discrimination at positive strength.

% DS08
Observational equivalence is a substantive limit: different reinforcement and heterogeneous processes can generate the same joint outcome distribution, including grouped observations \cite{gelastopoulos2025}. Even a valid contrast against B therefore cannot distinguish interaction from all non-interaction processes. Comparisons against C, D and E can narrow that interpretation only where their complete grids and zero-strength gates are valid.

% DS09
Signal-share values here define a synthetic response channel. Estimates from other items, modes or error models cannot be assigned to the SHP trust item without item-specific evidence \cite{antoun2026,lucasdonnellan2012}. The positioning search had limited coverage, so this draft makes no priority claim. The fixed compute close may also leave later tiers incomplete; those absences limit which cross-null comparisons can be discussed, even if the primary B tier completes.

Interior coverage was not established by the exploratory X6a primary joint-band reference against D1 in this artificial package. The available inventory, conditioning and reference-precision limits remain in the supplement.

Evaluation used new seeds after partial calibration exposure and protocol amendment. The gate passed; \resultnum{v4.inv.n_valid}{45} of 414 units finished valid. On \resultnum{v4.bd.n_eligible}{9} shared gap-free shares ($r=$ \resultnum{v4.bd.r_eligible}{0.50, 0.55, 0.60, 0.65, 0.70, 0.75, 0.80, 0.85, 0.90}), first boundaries against trait-plus-autoregressive/state-dependent persistence were small \resultnum{v4.bd.B.n_small}{9}/\resultnum{v4.bd.D.n_small}{0}, large \resultnum{v4.bd.B.n_large}{0}/\resultnum{v4.bd.D.n_large}{0}, not attained \resultnum{v4.bd.B.n_not_attained}{0}/\resultnum{v4.bd.D.n_not_attained}{9}, or censored/indeterminate \resultnum{v4.bd.B.n_censored}{0}/\resultnum{v4.bd.D.n_censored}{0}. At \resultnum{v4.bd.n_persistence}{9} of those shares this is compatible with non-Gaussian persistence, without specific evidence of interaction. The primary interpretation is conditional on the specified null family, response channel, panel design and fixed lag-feature discriminator. Attained boundaries on a complete valid curve will carry the frozen v1 labels: a small boundary ($0<a^*\le0.03$) would mean that this discriminator separates the declared synthetic laws at a small nominal strength, and a large one ($0.03<a^*\le0.90$) that separation requires a strength farther along the grid; the cut at 0.03 is an internal convention, not a demonstrated effect size. Gaps, edges or wide intervals make the affected region censored or indeterminate, and a zero-strength band that misses 0.5 invalidates the comparison at that value of $r$. Point crossings followed by lower AUCs must be distinguished from sustained crossings. Statements about how the boundary changes across $r$ are descriptive. No part of the curve identifies causal influence in a panel without observed exposure.

% DS02
The headline will report the comparisons against B and against D side by side whenever tier 2 is complete and valid. % DS03
The estimand is an oracle quantity. Both arms share a known signal share, so the null cannot adjust the response-channel noise variance. Estimation difficulties have been reported for trait--state--error decompositions \cite{cole2005tso,ludtke2018starts}. Each null is matched to population moments averaged over many simulated panels, not to one observed panel. Both arms also have time-invariant parameters and marginals, although the interaction arm starts without burn-in, and they share an exact response channel, mask and marginal, with attrition unrelated to opinion. Real panels can violate this through attrition related to the item, reliability that varies across waves, changes of mode or wording, period shocks and refreshment samples of different composition, any of which could by itself make two panel laws separable. % DS03 RC17

% Revised 2026-09-28 after the pre-results referee report. Markers DSxx map to
% rows in claim-evidence.md, section "Discussion (integrated 2026-09-28)".
% Open exploratory X5 estimates are stated; no confirmatory outcome is asserted.
% DS01
The primary interpretation is conditional on the specified null family, response channel, panel design and fixed lag-feature discriminator. Attained boundaries on a complete valid curve will carry the frozen v1 labels: a small boundary ($0<a^*\le0.03$) would mean that this discriminator separates the declared synthetic laws at a small nominal strength, and a large one ($0.03<a^*\le0.90$) that separation requires a strength farther along the grid; the cut at 0.03 is an internal convention, not a demonstrated effect size. A complete valid noncrossing would mean only that this discriminator did not attain the target on that grid; it would leave stronger inputs, other summaries and other classifiers unresolved. Gaps, edges or wide intervals make the affected region censored or indeterminate, and a zero-strength band that misses 0.5 invalidates the comparison at that value of $r$. Point crossings followed by lower AUCs must be distinguished from sustained crossings. Statements about how the boundary changes across $r$ are descriptive. No part of the curve identifies causal influence in a panel without observed exposure.

% DS02
The headline will report the comparisons against B and against D side by side whenever tier 2 is complete and valid. This pairing matters because, to first order, partner drift is a nonlinear function of a person's own state that pushes people away from the population centre, more strongly in the tails, so that after rank transport the interaction arm is a state-dependent persistence process, the class that D targets with a different functional form (Methods). If B crosses while D's valid upper band remains below the target, the frozen reading is that the result is compatible with non-Gaussian persistence and gives no specific evidence of interaction; a band spanning the target is inconclusive. A nonsignificant contrast does not establish equivalence. If tier 2 is incomplete at the close, the paper reports only the comparison against B and makes no cross-mechanism statement.

% DS03
The estimand is an oracle quantity. Both arms share a known signal share, so the null cannot adjust the response-channel noise variance. Estimation difficulties have been reported for trait--state--error decompositions \cite{cole2005tso,ludtke2018starts}. Each null is matched to population moments averaged over many simulated panels, not to one observed panel. The AUC target of 0.70 corresponds, under normal-theory assumptions, to a single-panel power of only about 0.18 (Table~\ref{tab:auc-translation}). A boundary is therefore a property of two laws at a known signal share, not a statement that an analyst holding one panel would detect partner drift at that strength. Both arms also have time-invariant parameters and marginals, although the interaction arm starts without burn-in, and they share an exact response channel, mask and marginal, with attrition unrelated to opinion. Real panels can violate this through attrition related to the item, reliability that varies across waves, changes of mode or wording, period shocks and refreshment samples of different composition, any of which could by itself make two panel laws separable. % DS03 RC17

The X5 misspecification comparison is unavailable in this artificial package because no X5 aggregate was supplied. This absence is not a null result.

% DS04
The generator is one fixed configuration: persistence 0.85, repulsion 0.25, eight random partners, no burn-in and one step per wave, with only attraction-only, anchoring and 24-step variants. Its rank transport removes the population-level signatures of bounded-confidence and repulsion models, so the boundary is not transferable to those models as usually understood. The interaction arm's lag profile has not been compared with that of the SHP item, so the panels share the survey's geometry but not necessarily its persistence. The SHP also records household co-residence, and household members aged 14 and older complete individual questionnaires \cite{voorpostel2025shp}; a household-coupled generator with a dyadic discriminator is left to future work.

% DS05
The SHP reliability anchor and the simulation's $r$ are different quantities. The anchor treats the 0--10 responses as continuous, whereas $r$ is a signal share before rank-based discretization. The anchor model is a latent autoregression without a stable trait, whereas null B has one; when a trait is present, simplex-type estimators attribute part of the long-lag plateau to the autoregression. For example, with latent lag correlations $0.5+0.5\cdot0.5^k$ and $r=0.70$, the Heise triplet estimate is about 0.63. The anchor wave, 2004, is the year the SHP added its first refreshment sample \cite{voorpostel2025shp}, which is also wave five of the synthetic geometry, so that wave mixes first interviews with continuing respondents. The anchor's interval is a model-based Wald interval, not a design-based one. The raw quasi-simplex anchor, the STARTS sensitivity and the synthetic compatibility map must therefore be presented separately. % DS05 RC24
The map depends on generator, strength and trait--state composition; its minimum--maximum ranges over ten synthetic replicates are not confidence intervals and do not propagate uncertainty in the empirical anchor. % DS05 RC25
It does not yield an empirically calibrated $a^*(r)$. % DS05 RC26

% DS06
Absolute interior coverage of the bands is not verified. The zero-strength gates test band mechanics where the nulls are exact by construction; G1b uses zero nuisance variance; G2 tests dispersion only; matching bias up to a quarter of the fitting standard error lies outside the variance; and the criteria's calibrated joint pass probability is not shown to reach 0.95. If the nine zero-strength gates of the main curve are independent and the procedure is correct, chance alone gives the main curve a probability of invalidation of up to about 5\%, in addition to invalidation by the compute close.

% DS07
The protocol was amended after partial calibration exposure, particularly at $r=0.70$. New seeds and sealed gate records constrain further adaptation but cannot make the resulting evaluation fully blind. Results at the other values of $r$ remain part of the prespecified whole curve; they cannot erase the method-level exposure. The v4 finite-law equality at zero strength is an identity of this simulator and random-number coupling. It does not imply equality of empirical mechanisms or guarantee discrimination at positive strength.

% DS08
Observational equivalence is a substantive limit: different reinforcement and heterogeneous processes can generate the same joint outcome distribution, including grouped observations \cite{gelastopoulos2025}. Even a valid contrast against B therefore cannot distinguish interaction from all non-interaction processes. Comparisons against C, D and E can narrow that interpretation only where their complete grids and zero-strength gates are valid.

% DS09
Signal-share values here define a synthetic response channel. Estimates from other items, modes or error models cannot be assigned to the SHP trust item without item-specific evidence \cite{antoun2026,lucasdonnellan2012}. The positioning search had limited coverage, so this draft makes no priority claim. The fixed compute close may also leave later tiers incomplete; those absences limit which cross-null comparisons can be discussed, even if the primary B tier completes.

Interior coverage was not established by the exploratory X6a primary joint-band reference against D1 in this artificial package. The available inventory, conditioning and reference-precision limits remain in the supplement.

cases.discussion:
% Revised 2026-09-28 after the pre-results referee report. Markers DSxx map to
% rows in claim-evidence.md, section "Discussion (integrated 2026-09-28)".
% Open exploratory X5 estimates are stated; no confirmatory outcome is asserted.
% DS01
The primary interpretation is conditional on the specified null family, response channel, panel design and fixed lag-feature discriminator. Attained boundaries on a complete valid curve will carry the frozen v1 labels: a small boundary ($0<a^*\le0.03$) would mean that this discriminator separates the declared synthetic laws at a small nominal strength, and a large one ($0.03<a^*\le0.90$) that separation requires a strength farther along the grid; the cut at 0.03 is an internal convention, not a demonstrated effect size. A complete valid noncrossing would mean only that this discriminator did not attain the target on that grid; it would leave stronger inputs, other summaries and other classifiers unresolved. Gaps, edges or wide intervals make the affected region censored or indeterminate, and a zero-strength band that misses 0.5 invalidates the comparison at that value of $r$. Point crossings followed by lower AUCs must be distinguished from sustained crossings. Statements about how the boundary changes across $r$ are descriptive. No part of the curve identifies causal influence in a panel without observed exposure.

% DS02
The headline will report the comparisons against B and against D side by side whenever tier 2 is complete and valid. This pairing matters because, to first order, partner drift is a nonlinear function of a person's own state that pushes people away from the population centre, more strongly in the tails, so that after rank transport the interaction arm is a state-dependent persistence process, the class that D targets with a different functional form (Methods). If B crosses while D's valid upper band remains below the target, the frozen reading is that the result is compatible with non-Gaussian persistence and gives no specific evidence of interaction; a band spanning the target is inconclusive. A nonsignificant contrast does not establish equivalence. If tier 2 is incomplete at the close, the paper reports only the comparison against B and makes no cross-mechanism statement.

% DS03
The estimand is an oracle quantity. Both arms share a known signal share, so the null cannot adjust the response-channel noise variance. Estimation difficulties have been reported for trait--state--error decompositions \cite{cole2005tso,ludtke2018starts}. Each null is matched to population moments averaged over many simulated panels, not to one observed panel. The AUC target of 0.70 corresponds, under normal-theory assumptions, to a single-panel power of only about 0.18 (Table~\ref{tab:auc-translation}). A boundary is therefore a property of two laws at a known signal share, not a statement that an analyst holding one panel would detect partner drift at that strength. Both arms also have time-invariant parameters and marginals, although the interaction arm starts without burn-in, and they share an exact response channel, mask and marginal, with attrition unrelated to opinion. Real panels can violate this through attrition related to the item, reliability that varies across waves, changes of mode or wording, period shocks and refreshment samples of different composition, any of which could by itself make two panel laws separable. % DS03 RC17

The X5 misspecification comparison is unavailable in this artificial package because no X5 aggregate was supplied. This absence is not a null result.

% DS04
The generator is one fixed configuration: persistence 0.85, repulsion 0.25, eight random partners, no burn-in and one step per wave, with only attraction-only, anchoring and 24-step variants. Its rank transport removes the population-level signatures of bounded-confidence and repulsion models, so the boundary is not transferable to those models as usually understood. The interaction arm's lag profile has not been compared with that of the SHP item, so the panels share the survey's geometry but not necessarily its persistence. The SHP also records household co-residence, and household members aged 14 and older complete individual questionnaires \cite{voorpostel2025shp}; a household-coupled generator with a dyadic discriminator is left to future work.

% DS05
The SHP reliability anchor and the simulation's $r$ are different quantities. The anchor treats the 0--10 responses as continuous, whereas $r$ is a signal share before rank-based discretization. The anchor model is a latent autoregression without a stable trait, whereas null B has one; when a trait is present, simplex-type estimators attribute part of the long-lag plateau to the autoregression. For example, with latent lag correlations $0.5+0.5\cdot0.5^k$ and $r=0.70$, the Heise triplet estimate is about 0.63. The anchor wave, 2004, is the year the SHP added its first refreshment sample \cite{voorpostel2025shp}, which is also wave five of the synthetic geometry, so that wave mixes first interviews with continuing respondents. The anchor's interval is a model-based Wald interval, not a design-based one. The raw quasi-simplex anchor, the STARTS sensitivity and the synthetic compatibility map must therefore be presented separately. % DS05 RC24
The map depends on generator, strength and trait--state composition; its minimum--maximum ranges over ten synthetic replicates are not confidence intervals and do not propagate uncertainty in the empirical anchor. % DS05 RC25
It does not yield an empirically calibrated $a^*(r)$. % DS05 RC26

% DS06
Absolute interior coverage of the bands is not verified. The zero-strength gates test band mechanics where the nulls are exact by construction; G1b uses zero nuisance variance; G2 tests dispersion only; matching bias up to a quarter of the fitting standard error lies outside the variance; and the criteria's calibrated joint pass probability is not shown to reach 0.95. If the nine zero-strength gates of the main curve are independent and the procedure is correct, chance alone gives the main curve a probability of invalidation of up to about 5\%, in addition to invalidation by the compute close.

% DS07
The protocol was amended after partial calibration exposure, particularly at $r=0.70$. New seeds and sealed gate records constrain further adaptation but cannot make the resulting evaluation fully blind. Results at the other values of $r$ remain part of the prespecified whole curve; they cannot erase the method-level exposure. The v4 finite-law equality at zero strength is an identity of this simulator and random-number coupling. It does not imply equality of empirical mechanisms or guarantee discrimination at positive strength.

% DS08
Observational equivalence is a substantive limit: different reinforcement and heterogeneous processes can generate the same joint outcome distribution, including grouped observations \cite{gelastopoulos2025}. Even a valid contrast against B therefore cannot distinguish interaction from all non-interaction processes. Comparisons against C, D and E can narrow that interpretation only where their complete grids and zero-strength gates are valid.

% DS09
Signal-share values here define a synthetic response channel. Estimates from other items, modes or error models cannot be assigned to the SHP trust item without item-specific evidence \cite{antoun2026,lucasdonnellan2012}. The positioning search had limited coverage, so this draft makes no priority claim. The fixed compute close may also leave later tiers incomplete; those absences limit which cross-null comparisons can be discussed, even if the primary B tier completes.

Interior coverage was not established by the exploratory X6a primary joint-band reference against D1 in this artificial package. The available inventory, conditioning and reference-precision limits remain in the supplement.

cases.abstract: Opinion panels can resemble partner drift or persistence when exposure is unobserved. We evaluate a synthetic detection boundary for a fixed lag-based discriminator against matched no-network persistence. An eleven-wave rank-transported autoregression combines bounded-confidence-shaped drift and an unobserved random network; first-order drift depends on individual state. Panels use Swiss Household Panel geometry and a response signal share known to both arms. Nulls match short-lag population moments. The primary estimand is the curve of first grid strengths whose expected AUC against trait-plus-autoregressive persistence reaches 0.70. % Revised 2026-09-28 after the pre-results referee report. Markers DSxx map to
% rows in claim-evidence.md, section "Discussion (integrated 2026-09-28)".
% Open exploratory X5 estimates are stated; no confirmatory outcome is asserted.
% DS01
The primary interpretation is conditional on the specified null family, response channel, panel design and fixed lag-feature discriminator. Attained boundaries on a complete valid curve will carry the frozen v1 labels: a small boundary ($0<a^*\le0.03$) would mean that this discriminator separates the declared synthetic laws at a small nominal strength, and a large one ($0.03<a^*\le0.90$) that separation requires a strength farther along the grid; the cut at 0.03 is an internal convention, not a demonstrated effect size. A complete valid noncrossing would mean only that this discriminator did not attain the target on that grid; it would leave stronger inputs, other summaries and other classifiers unresolved. Gaps, edges or wide intervals make the affected region censored or indeterminate, and a zero-strength band that misses 0.5 invalidates the comparison at that value of $r$. Point crossings followed by lower AUCs must be distinguished from sustained crossings. Statements about how the boundary changes across $r$ are descriptive. No part of the curve identifies causal influence in a panel without observed exposure.

% DS02
The headline will report the comparisons against B and against D side by side whenever tier 2 is complete and valid. This pairing matters because, to first order, partner drift is a nonlinear function of a person's own state that pushes people away from the population centre, more strongly in the tails, so that after rank transport the interaction arm is a state-dependent persistence process, the class that D targets with a different functional form (Methods). If B crosses while D's valid upper band remains below the target, the frozen reading is that the result is compatible with non-Gaussian persistence and gives no specific evidence of interaction; a band spanning the target is inconclusive. A nonsignificant contrast does not establish equivalence. If tier 2 is incomplete at the close, the paper reports only the comparison against B and makes no cross-mechanism statement.

% DS03
The estimand is an oracle quantity. Both arms share a known signal share, so the null cannot adjust the response-channel noise variance. Estimation difficulties have been reported for trait--state--error decompositions \cite{cole2005tso,ludtke2018starts}. Each null is matched to population moments averaged over many simulated panels, not to one observed panel. The AUC target of 0.70 corresponds, under normal-theory assumptions, to a single-panel power of only about 0.18 (Table~\ref{tab:auc-translation}). A boundary is therefore a property of two laws at a known signal share, not a statement that an analyst holding one panel would detect partner drift at that strength. Both arms also have time-invariant parameters and marginals, although the interaction arm starts without burn-in, and they share an exact response channel, mask and marginal, with attrition unrelated to opinion. Real panels can violate this through attrition related to the item, reliability that varies across waves, changes of mode or wording, period shocks and refreshment samples of different composition, any of which could by itself make two panel laws separable. % DS03 RC17

The X5 misspecification comparison is unavailable in this artificial package because no X5 aggregate was supplied. This absence is not a null result.

% DS04
The generator is one fixed configuration: persistence 0.85, repulsion 0.25, eight random partners, no burn-in and one step per wave, with only attraction-only, anchoring and 24-step variants. Its rank transport removes the population-level signatures of bounded-confidence and repulsion models, so the boundary is not transferable to those models as usually understood. The interaction arm's lag profile has not been compared with that of the SHP item, so the panels share the survey's geometry but not necessarily its persistence. The SHP also records household co-residence, and household members aged 14 and older complete individual questionnaires \cite{voorpostel2025shp}; a household-coupled generator with a dyadic discriminator is left to future work.

% DS05
The SHP reliability anchor and the simulation's $r$ are different quantities. The anchor treats the 0--10 responses as continuous, whereas $r$ is a signal share before rank-based discretization. The anchor model is a latent autoregression without a stable trait, whereas null B has one; when a trait is present, simplex-type estimators attribute part of the long-lag plateau to the autoregression. For example, with latent lag correlations $0.5+0.5\cdot0.5^k$ and $r=0.70$, the Heise triplet estimate is about 0.63. The anchor wave, 2004, is the year the SHP added its first refreshment sample \cite{voorpostel2025shp}, which is also wave five of the synthetic geometry, so that wave mixes first interviews with continuing respondents. The anchor's interval is a model-based Wald interval, not a design-based one. The raw quasi-simplex anchor, the STARTS sensitivity and the synthetic compatibility map must therefore be presented separately. % DS05 RC24
The map depends on generator, strength and trait--state composition; its minimum--maximum ranges over ten synthetic replicates are not confidence intervals and do not propagate uncertainty in the empirical anchor. % DS05 RC25
It does not yield an empirically calibrated $a^*(r)$. % DS05 RC26

% DS06
Absolute interior coverage of the bands is not verified. The zero-strength gates test band mechanics where the nulls are exact by construction; G1b uses zero nuisance variance; G2 tests dispersion only; matching bias up to a quarter of the fitting standard error lies outside the variance; and the criteria's calibrated joint pass probability is not shown to reach 0.95. If the nine zero-strength gates of the main curve are independent and the procedure is correct, chance alone gives the main curve a probability of invalidation of up to about 5\%, in addition to invalidation by the compute close.

% DS07
The protocol was amended after partial calibration exposure, particularly at $r=0.70$. New seeds and sealed gate records constrain further adaptation but cannot make the resulting evaluation fully blind. Results at the other values of $r$ remain part of the prespecified whole curve; they cannot erase the method-level exposure. The v4 finite-law equality at zero strength is an identity of this simulator and random-number coupling. It does not imply equality of empirical mechanisms or guarantee discrimination at positive strength.

% DS08
Observational equivalence is a substantive limit: different reinforcement and heterogeneous processes can generate the same joint outcome distribution, including grouped observations \cite{gelastopoulos2025}. Even a valid contrast against B therefore cannot distinguish interaction from all non-interaction processes. Comparisons against C, D and E can narrow that interpretation only where their complete grids and zero-strength gates are valid.

% DS09
Signal-share values here define a synthetic response channel. Estimates from other items, modes or error models cannot be assigned to the SHP trust item without item-specific evidence \cite{antoun2026,lucasdonnellan2012}. The positioning search had limited coverage, so this draft makes no priority claim. The fixed compute close may also leave later tiers incomplete; those absences limit which cross-null comparisons can be discussed, even if the primary B tier completes.

The exploratory X6a primary joint-band reference against D1 had the machine reading \resultnum{v4x.x6.x6a.band.vs_d1.primary.reading}{subnominal}. Interior coverage was below nominal under the declared criterion; the full numerator, denominator, Wilson interval and precision sensitivity remain in the exploratory supplement.

% Revised 2026-09-28 after the pre-results referee report. Markers DSxx map to
% rows in claim-evidence.md, section "Discussion (integrated 2026-09-28)".
% Open exploratory X5 estimates are stated; no confirmatory outcome is asserted.
% DS01
The primary interpretation is conditional on the specified null family, response channel, panel design and fixed lag-feature discriminator. Attained boundaries on a complete valid curve will carry the frozen v1 labels: a small boundary ($0<a^*\le0.03$) would mean that this discriminator separates the declared synthetic laws at a small nominal strength, and a large one ($0.03<a^*\le0.90$) that separation requires a strength farther along the grid; the cut at 0.03 is an internal convention, not a demonstrated effect size. A complete valid noncrossing would mean only that this discriminator did not attain the target on that grid; it would leave stronger inputs, other summaries and other classifiers unresolved. Gaps, edges or wide intervals make the affected region censored or indeterminate, and a zero-strength band that misses 0.5 invalidates the comparison at that value of $r$. Point crossings followed by lower AUCs must be distinguished from sustained crossings. Statements about how the boundary changes across $r$ are descriptive. No part of the curve identifies causal influence in a panel without observed exposure.

% DS02
The headline will report the comparisons against B and against D side by side whenever tier 2 is complete and valid. This pairing matters because, to first order, partner drift is a nonlinear function of a person's own state that pushes people away from the population centre, more strongly in the tails, so that after rank transport the interaction arm is a state-dependent persistence process, the class that D targets with a different functional form (Methods). If B crosses while D's valid upper band remains below the target, the frozen reading is that the result is compatible with non-Gaussian persistence and gives no specific evidence of interaction; a band spanning the target is inconclusive. A nonsignificant contrast does not establish equivalence. If tier 2 is incomplete at the close, the paper reports only the comparison against B and makes no cross-mechanism statement.

% DS03
The estimand is an oracle quantity. Both arms share a known signal share, so the null cannot adjust the response-channel noise variance. Estimation difficulties have been reported for trait--state--error decompositions \cite{cole2005tso,ludtke2018starts}. Each null is matched to population moments averaged over many simulated panels, not to one observed panel. The AUC target of 0.70 corresponds, under normal-theory assumptions, to a single-panel power of only about 0.18 (Table~\ref{tab:auc-translation}). A boundary is therefore a property of two laws at a known signal share, not a statement that an analyst holding one panel would detect partner drift at that strength. Both arms also have time-invariant parameters and marginals, although the interaction arm starts without burn-in, and they share an exact response channel, mask and marginal, with attrition unrelated to opinion. Real panels can violate this through attrition related to the item, reliability that varies across waves, changes of mode or wording, period shocks and refreshment samples of different composition, any of which could by itself make two panel laws separable. % DS03 RC17

The X5 misspecification comparison is unavailable in this artificial package because no X5 aggregate was supplied. This absence is not a null result.

% DS04
The generator is one fixed configuration: persistence 0.85, repulsion 0.25, eight random partners, no burn-in and one step per wave, with only attraction-only, anchoring and 24-step variants. Its rank transport removes the population-level signatures of bounded-confidence and repulsion models, so the boundary is not transferable to those models as usually understood. The interaction arm's lag profile has not been compared with that of the SHP item, so the panels share the survey's geometry but not necessarily its persistence. The SHP also records household co-residence, and household members aged 14 and older complete individual questionnaires \cite{voorpostel2025shp}; a household-coupled generator with a dyadic discriminator is left to future work.

% DS05
The SHP reliability anchor and the simulation's $r$ are different quantities. The anchor treats the 0--10 responses as continuous, whereas $r$ is a signal share before rank-based discretization. The anchor model is a latent autoregression without a stable trait, whereas null B has one; when a trait is present, simplex-type estimators attribute part of the long-lag plateau to the autoregression. For example, with latent lag correlations $0.5+0.5\cdot0.5^k$ and $r=0.70$, the Heise triplet estimate is about 0.63. The anchor wave, 2004, is the year the SHP added its first refreshment sample \cite{voorpostel2025shp}, which is also wave five of the synthetic geometry, so that wave mixes first interviews with continuing respondents. The anchor's interval is a model-based Wald interval, not a design-based one. The raw quasi-simplex anchor, the STARTS sensitivity and the synthetic compatibility map must therefore be presented separately. % DS05 RC24
The map depends on generator, strength and trait--state composition; its minimum--maximum ranges over ten synthetic replicates are not confidence intervals and do not propagate uncertainty in the empirical anchor. % DS05 RC25
It does not yield an empirically calibrated $a^*(r)$. % DS05 RC26

% DS06
Absolute interior coverage of the bands is not verified. The zero-strength gates test band mechanics where the nulls are exact by construction; G1b uses zero nuisance variance; G2 tests dispersion only; matching bias up to a quarter of the fitting standard error lies outside the variance; and the criteria's calibrated joint pass probability is not shown to reach 0.95. If the nine zero-strength gates of the main curve are independent and the procedure is correct, chance alone gives the main curve a probability of invalidation of up to about 5\%, in addition to invalidation by the compute close.

% DS07
The protocol was amended after partial calibration exposure, particularly at $r=0.70$. New seeds and sealed gate records constrain further adaptation but cannot make the resulting evaluation fully blind. Results at the other values of $r$ remain part of the prespecified whole curve; they cannot erase the method-level exposure. The v4 finite-law equality at zero strength is an identity of this simulator and random-number coupling. It does not imply equality of empirical mechanisms or guarantee discrimination at positive strength.

% DS08
Observational equivalence is a substantive limit: different reinforcement and heterogeneous processes can generate the same joint outcome distribution, including grouped observations \cite{gelastopoulos2025}. Even a valid contrast against B therefore cannot distinguish interaction from all non-interaction processes. Comparisons against C, D and E can narrow that interpretation only where their complete grids and zero-strength gates are valid.

% DS09
Signal-share values here define a synthetic response channel. Estimates from other items, modes or error models cannot be assigned to the SHP trust item without item-specific evidence \cite{antoun2026,lucasdonnellan2012}. The positioning search had limited coverage, so this draft makes no priority claim. The fixed compute close may also leave later tiers incomplete; those absences limit which cross-null comparisons can be discussed, even if the primary B tier completes.

The exploratory X6a primary joint-band reference against D1 had the machine reading \resultnum{v4x.x6.x6a.band.vs_d1.primary.reading}{failure}. Interior coverage was below nominal under the declared criterion; the full numerator, denominator, Wilson interval and precision sensitivity remain in the exploratory supplement.

% Revised 2026-09-28 after the pre-results referee report. Markers DSxx map to
% rows in claim-evidence.md, section "Discussion (integrated 2026-09-28)".
% Open exploratory X5 estimates are stated; no confirmatory outcome is asserted.
% DS01
The primary interpretation is conditional on the specified null family, response channel, panel design and fixed lag-feature discriminator. Attained boundaries on a complete valid curve will carry the frozen v1 labels: a small boundary ($0<a^*\le0.03$) would mean that this discriminator separates the declared synthetic laws at a small nominal strength, and a large one ($0.03<a^*\le0.90$) that separation requires a strength farther along the grid; the cut at 0.03 is an internal convention, not a demonstrated effect size. A complete valid noncrossing would mean only that this discriminator did not attain the target on that grid; it would leave stronger inputs, other summaries and other classifiers unresolved. Gaps, edges or wide intervals make the affected region censored or indeterminate, and a zero-strength band that misses 0.5 invalidates the comparison at that value of $r$. Point crossings followed by lower AUCs must be distinguished from sustained crossings. Statements about how the boundary changes across $r$ are descriptive. No part of the curve identifies causal influence in a panel without observed exposure.

% DS02
The headline will report the comparisons against B and against D side by side whenever tier 2 is complete and valid. This pairing matters because, to first order, partner drift is a nonlinear function of a person's own state that pushes people away from the population centre, more strongly in the tails, so that after rank transport the interaction arm is a state-dependent persistence process, the class that D targets with a different functional form (Methods). If B crosses while D's valid upper band remains below the target, the frozen reading is that the result is compatible with non-Gaussian persistence and gives no specific evidence of interaction; a band spanning the target is inconclusive. A nonsignificant contrast does not establish equivalence. If tier 2 is incomplete at the close, the paper reports only the comparison against B and makes no cross-mechanism statement.

% DS03
The estimand is an oracle quantity. Both arms share a known signal share, so the null cannot adjust the response-channel noise variance. Estimation difficulties have been reported for trait--state--error decompositions \cite{cole2005tso,ludtke2018starts}. Each null is matched to population moments averaged over many simulated panels, not to one observed panel. The AUC target of 0.70 corresponds, under normal-theory assumptions, to a single-panel power of only about 0.18 (Table~\ref{tab:auc-translation}). A boundary is therefore a property of two laws at a known signal share, not a statement that an analyst holding one panel would detect partner drift at that strength. Both arms also have time-invariant parameters and marginals, although the interaction arm starts without burn-in, and they share an exact response channel, mask and marginal, with attrition unrelated to opinion. Real panels can violate this through attrition related to the item, reliability that varies across waves, changes of mode or wording, period shocks and refreshment samples of different composition, any of which could by itself make two panel laws separable. % DS03 RC17

The X5 misspecification comparison is unavailable in this artificial package because no X5 aggregate was supplied. This absence is not a null result.

% DS04
The generator is one fixed configuration: persistence 0.85, repulsion 0.25, eight random partners, no burn-in and one step per wave, with only attraction-only, anchoring and 24-step variants. Its rank transport removes the population-level signatures of bounded-confidence and repulsion models, so the boundary is not transferable to those models as usually understood. The interaction arm's lag profile has not been compared with that of the SHP item, so the panels share the survey's geometry but not necessarily its persistence. The SHP also records household co-residence, and household members aged 14 and older complete individual questionnaires \cite{voorpostel2025shp}; a household-coupled generator with a dyadic discriminator is left to future work.

% DS05
The SHP reliability anchor and the simulation's $r$ are different quantities. The anchor treats the 0--10 responses as continuous, whereas $r$ is a signal share before rank-based discretization. The anchor model is a latent autoregression without a stable trait, whereas null B has one; when a trait is present, simplex-type estimators attribute part of the long-lag plateau to the autoregression. For example, with latent lag correlations $0.5+0.5\cdot0.5^k$ and $r=0.70$, the Heise triplet estimate is about 0.63. The anchor wave, 2004, is the year the SHP added its first refreshment sample \cite{voorpostel2025shp}, which is also wave five of the synthetic geometry, so that wave mixes first interviews with continuing respondents. The anchor's interval is a model-based Wald interval, not a design-based one. The raw quasi-simplex anchor, the STARTS sensitivity and the synthetic compatibility map must therefore be presented separately. % DS05 RC24
The map depends on generator, strength and trait--state composition; its minimum--maximum ranges over ten synthetic replicates are not confidence intervals and do not propagate uncertainty in the empirical anchor. % DS05 RC25
It does not yield an empirically calibrated $a^*(r)$. % DS05 RC26

% DS06
Absolute interior coverage of the bands is not verified. The zero-strength gates test band mechanics where the nulls are exact by construction; G1b uses zero nuisance variance; G2 tests dispersion only; matching bias up to a quarter of the fitting standard error lies outside the variance; and the criteria's calibrated joint pass probability is not shown to reach 0.95. If the nine zero-strength gates of the main curve are independent and the procedure is correct, chance alone gives the main curve a probability of invalidation of up to about 5\%, in addition to invalidation by the compute close.

% DS07
The protocol was amended after partial calibration exposure, particularly at $r=0.70$. New seeds and sealed gate records constrain further adaptation but cannot make the resulting evaluation fully blind. Results at the other values of $r$ remain part of the prespecified whole curve; they cannot erase the method-level exposure. The v4 finite-law equality at zero strength is an identity of this simulator and random-number coupling. It does not imply equality of empirical mechanisms or guarantee discrimination at positive strength.

% DS08
Observational equivalence is a substantive limit: different reinforcement and heterogeneous processes can generate the same joint outcome distribution, including grouped observations \cite{gelastopoulos2025}. Even a valid contrast against B therefore cannot distinguish interaction from all non-interaction processes. Comparisons against C, D and E can narrow that interpretation only where their complete grids and zero-strength gates are valid.

% DS09
Signal-share values here define a synthetic response channel. Estimates from other items, modes or error models cannot be assigned to the SHP trust item without item-specific evidence \cite{antoun2026,lucasdonnellan2012}. The positioning search had limited coverage, so this draft makes no priority claim. The fixed compute close may also leave later tiers incomplete; those absences limit which cross-null comparisons can be discussed, even if the primary B tier completes.

Interior coverage was not established by the exploratory X6a primary joint-band reference against D1 in this artificial package. The available inventory, conditioning and reference-precision limits remain in the supplement.

cases.abstract: Opinion panels can resemble partner drift or persistence when exposure is unobserved. We evaluate a synthetic detection boundary for a fixed lag-based discriminator against matched no-network persistence. An eleven-wave rank-transported autoregression combines bounded-confidence-shaped drift and an unobserved random network; first-order drift depends on individual state. Panels use Swiss Household Panel geometry and a response signal share known to both arms. Nulls match short-lag population moments. The primary estimand is the curve of first grid strengths whose expected AUC against trait-plus-autoregressive persistence reaches 0.70. Every stage must pass before any evaluation on reserved seeds. The six-stage validation gate failed at its last stage, which compares local nuisance propagation with full refits, so no confirmatory seed was derived and no curve was estimated. Under the frozen rules, any continuation requires a new, separately frozen protocol with cumulative exposure. Separation is conditional on the declared laws, response channel and discriminator and does not identify causal social influence.
